summary: Based only on on-screen events EP48:E1 to EP48:E43 in scenes sc_001 and sc_002, Catherine privately plans to counter Alexander and the council during a ten-day window. She has Agnes lock the door, sends Agnes with a purse to summon a priest secretly, and says she will return to the house rather than flee. Uncertainty: sc_002 has incomplete source coverage with gaps unavailable, so events between the recorded timestamps may be missing. Father Thomas, Alexander and the Duke appear only in dialogue or are referenced; none is seen on screen. Juliana is not named in on-screen events. Intent and the identity of the crown referenced in dialogue are inferred from dialogue only. Metadata was not used as evidence; its account of a prior public humiliation and the reprieve is unseen in this source.

beats.description: Catherine stands at the window in her chamber at night and turns with a cold smirk.
Catherine speaks of using the ten-day period for the council, witnesses and a decree, and frames the period as a door that can be closed from the other side.
Agnes enters on Catherine's summons and the chamber door is locked with an iron key.
Catherine grips Agnes's hands and expresses resentment over her public humiliation, saying grief makes the household careless.
Agnes warns of bailiffs on the roads and Catherine replies that she will go back into the house instead of leaving the county.
Catherine says Father Thomas has already done his part and needs to do more, and orders that no one see him come to her.
Catherine gives Agnes a heavy purse, orders her to send for the priest tonight without being seen, and Agnes hurries out.
Through the window, Catherine stands motionless in candlelight staring into the night as the scene fades to black.
